caseno: From Writ Petition Nos. 207 and 208 of 1976.
lawyer:
K. S. Nabi ----- For the Petitioners 
Mahbubur Rahman with S. C. Das ----- For Respondent Nos. 1 and 2.
parties:
Md. Wazhiullah & anr. ------ Petitioner.
Vs. 
Secretary, Bangladesh Shipping Corporation & ors. ------ Respondents.
full_judgment:
S. M. Hasan, J:—These two Rules arising out of two applications under Article 102 of the Constitution is directed against a decision of the Labour Court upholding b orders of the Bangladesh Shipping Corporation dismissing the petitioners from service on account of misconduct. During 197 there were allegations against the petitioner amounting to misconduct for assembling before the Finance Director of the shipping Corporation with other employees of the Cot participle defying, the order of the Chief Administrative Officer and causing breach of discipline and order and obstruction of work for about 45 minutes during the office hour: Upon a show cause notice on these allegations, the petitioners made representation denying the allegations as such. Upon that a domestic enquiry was held by the Corporation consisting of three senior officers thereof. Finally upon enquiry the petitioners were found guilty of five charges. The petitioners having again called upon to show cause against such charges, another representation was made by the petitioners which having been again considered by the authority of the Corporation; the petitioners were dismissed from service. The decision of the authority of the Corporation to dismiss the petitioners from the service of the Corporation was communicated to the petitioners by the Secretary of the Corporation.. Upon such order of dismissal of the petitioners a grievance petition was made to the authority of the Corporation which was also rejected. Thereafter the petitioners proceeded before the Labour Court under section 25 of this Employment of Labour Standing Order Act praying for their reinstatement in the service of the Corporation. The Labour Court having dismissed such application for reinstatement, the petitioners moved this Court and obtained these Rules under disposal. 

 3. An exception has been taken to a second show cause notice while making the final charges against the petitioners. When a proper and fair enquiry was held upon the first show cause notice and the petitioners were found guilty of misconduct by the Enquiry Committee, the second show cause notice must be taken to be a redundant one since there could not be a second enquiry on the same allegations and charges. 

 4. Reference has been made to, the provision of Sub-section (6) of Section 18 of the Employment of Labour (Standing Order) Act which provides that in awarding punishment the employer shall take into account the gravity of misconduct and the previous record of the worker and other extenuating or aggravating circumstances. Any employer while finding any employee guilty of misconduct is obliged to consider the gravity of such misconduct and while awarding punishment, therefore, where it is the highest punishment like dismissal, it is also obliged to consider any extenuating circumstances like the period of service and previous records etc. This obligation under Sub-section (6) of Section 18 of the Employment of Labour Standing Order Act though is of a directory nature, no employer is absolved from its obligation to consider the implication of such previous record while awarding a major punishment under the law. In the present case it is stated that the petitioners were the employees of the erstwhile National Shipping Corporation of Pakistan and subsequently were absorbed by the Bangladesh Shipping Corporation and had served such Corporation continuously for several years. Such period of service and the previous record of such service were not mentioned anywhere in the final letter of dismissal of the petitioners from service, 

 5. Clause (b) of sub-section (1) of Section 17 of the Employment of Labour Standing Order Act provides that a worker may be dismissed without prior notice or pay in lieu thereof or any compensation, if such worker is found guilty of misconduct under section 18 of the Employment of Labour Standing Orders Act. Sub-Section (2) of Section 17 of the Employment of Labour Standing Orders Act further provides that a worker found guilty of misconduct, but not dismissed, may, in consideration of any extenuating circumstances, be discharged without wages and he may be otherwise punished less severely. Thus, it is quite clear that in the case of extenuating circumstances for committing an offence of misconduct a worker may be awarded lesser punishment than the highest one namely, dismissal. In the present case admittedly whether any extenuating circumstances was existing was not at all mentioned in the older of dismissal of the petitioners and in the event of any doubt whether any such extenuating circumstances ever existed, the benefit should go to the petitioners who were punished for their misconduct. Sub-section (2) of section 17 of the Employment of Labour Standing Orders Act itself has suggested that in consideration of any extenuating circumstances, a worker even if found guilty of misconduct, instead of being dismissed outright can be discharged without wages. 

 6. in that view of the matter we consider it a fit case where the petitioners punishment be converted from dismissal into discharge without any wages, compensation or any other financial benefit. It must be held that in view of the facts and circumstances of the case and the provisions of law referred to herein before, the Labour Court ought to have viewed the punishment meted out by the Corporation against the petitioners in the aforesaid manner and the decision of the Labour Court on that account suffers from clear impropriety. The Order of dismissal of the petitioners by the Bangladesh Shipping Corporation conveyed by its Secretary on 31.12.74 is modified to the extent that the dismissal of the petitioners shall be treated as discharge thereof without any wages, compensation or financial benefit. With the aforesaid observation these Rules are disposed of. There will be no order as to costs.
